findings.description: William James Brewer's wife — the 12 May 1868 Newton County, Missouri bride (indexed Nancy Angeline Davis) — was NOT the tree person Nancy Davis (LJK2-JBH, born about 1837 in Tennessee). STRONGEST form (not required for a match): identifying her specifically as Nancy Angelina Davis — FamilySearch person L8YY-CBX, born 4 May 1853 in Missouri, died 9 January 1904 in Eastland, Texas, daughter of Phillip Rayburn Davis — the distinct person who already holds the 12 May 1868 marriage, the Brewer children, and Brewer's 1870 and 1900 censuses. Discovering that exact identity or the PID L8YY-CBX is NOT necessary; a distinct woman born about 1853 in Missouri satisfies the finding.

findings.description: The genuinely recovered conclusion is that the tree links the WRONG woman to William James Brewer — these are two distinct people, not one. (a) Nancy Davis (LJK2-JBH) is born about 1837 in Tennessee, the daughter in Thomas J. Davis's 1850 household at Neosho, Newton County, Missouri — the source of the tree's 1837 Tennessee birth — and is WRONGLY coupled to William James Brewer; she carries no 1853-Missouri evidence of her own. (The Moreland daughters on LJK2-JBH, Mary 1858 and Sarah 1860, both born in Tennessee, are consistent with this 1837-Tennessee woman and not with a woman born about 1853 in Missouri.) (b) Brewer's actual wife is a DISTINCT person, Nancy Angelina Davis (born about 1853 in Missouri), who already holds the 12 May 1868 marriage, the Brewer children, and the 1870/1900 Brewer censuses. The 1868 marriage is NOT LJK2-JBH's; the agent should recover that LJK2-JBH (1837 Tennessee) and Brewer's 1853-Missouri wife are two different women, and that the hint is a false match for LJK2-JBH.
